subject: Private Offer structure and channel hurdle for CloudLeap – bundling options
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy@cloudleap.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudLeap Procurement <procurement@cloudleap.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing for multi-cloud private offer (AWS + GCP)

Hi Vivek,

Following up from our call — CloudLeap is evaluating a private offer across AWS and GCP for a new AI feature set we plan to ship H1 next year. We want to understand:

- How you would structure a private offer that includes both hosted API usage (per-token gen) and a dedicated Reserved capacity SKU for predictable throughput.
- Our procurement team needs to see list prices, suggested SKU anchors for marketplace, and an explicit channel margin/pass-through for our reseller (they typically expect a 12% pass-through).
- We can commit to an initial 12-month minimum $350k ARR across both clouds, with a potential step-up to $700k at year-end if adoption hits targets.

Can you share a sample pricing waterfall (list price -> private-offer discount -> channel pass-through) and confirm whether Redwood can map a tiered channel margin that changes with committed ARR?

Please also include any required paperwork/turnaround time for private offer setup in both marketplaces. Attaching our internal usage snapshot (cloudleap-proposed-commit.csv) for context.

Thanks — appreciate a short turnaround on this.

Amy Chen
Head of Strategic Procurement
CloudLeap

Attachment: cloudleap-proposed-commit.csv (CSV)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@cloudleap.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing for multi-cloud private offer (AWS + GCP)

Amy — thanks for the data and the clarity on commit range. High-level answers and next steps below.

1) Structure we recommend
- Two-part private offer: Marketplace SKUs for (a) Hosted API (consumption) and (b) Reserved Dedicated capacity (monthly commitment). Private offer will list both SKUs so CloudLeap can route traffic appropriately.
- We propose a tiered discount band tied to committed ARR: 0-$350k (base), $350k-$700k (growth band), 700k+ (enterprise uplift).

2) Channel pass-through approach
- Redwood supports explicit channel pass-through on private offers. Typical pass-through we see ranges from 10–18% depending on list price cushions and commit.
- Given your ask of 12% pass-through, we can model an initial pass-through of 12% on Year 1 if CloudLeap signs the $350k ARR commit. We can increase the pass-through to 14% once commit ramps to $700k.

3) Marketplace anchors & list price guidance
- We'll provide suggested SKU anchors and list-price deltas for AWS and GCP marketplaces. These are usually a list-price floor + private-offer discount that preserves margin for both Redwood and your reseller.

4) Timing and paperwork
- Once terms agreed, private offer creation typically takes 5–10 business days (depends on marketplace and AWS/GCP PO approvals). DocuSign for Master Purchase Agreement + PO often expedites it.

I've attached an initial scenario workbook (RLX-pricing-scenarios.xlsx) that walks through three waterfall scenarios (conservative / target / aggressive) and shows the channel margin at each tier. Can you confirm the split you expect between consumption vs reserved (approx % of ARR)? That will help us firm the split and list prices.

Next steps: quick 30-minute sync early next week to align on commit cadence and reseller crediting flow (how CloudLeap wants pass-through applied — as a separate rebate line vs embedded in private-offer discount).

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, GTM Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RLX-pricing-scenarios.xlsx (Excel)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: CloudLeap pricing — internal proposal

Internal note — forwarding CloudLeap's thread. My quick take and numbers to drop into the workbook:

- If they commit $350k ARR and expect 12% reseller pass-through, we can still hit target unit economics with these assumptions: 15% private-offer gross discount, 12% reseller pass-through, ~8% effective cost after batching/quantization for hosted.
- Proposal: anchor list price so that private-offer discount + 12% pass-through nets Redwood ~20% margin on list. If they move to $700k, increase pass-through to 14% and shift 2% more to reserved SKU rebates.

Suggested waterfall (example):
- List price (hosted): $0.025 per 1k tokens
- Private-offer discount (conservative): 40% -> effective price to customer $0.015 per 1k tokens
- Channel pass-through: 12% of list price ($0.003 per 1k) paid to reseller or embedded in private offer
- Effective to Redwood after pass-through: $0.012 per 1k tokens

Notes: need legal to confirm pass-through language — whether it is executed as a marketplace rebate (preferred) or vendor credit (more manual).

I'll mark the workbook with these numbers. We should be explicit in the DocuSign PO language about the pass-through calculation and the condition for increasing pass-through at the $700k milestone.

—Ben

Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer structure and channel hurdle for CloudLeap – bundling options

Thanks for the quick review, Vivek / Ben. A few clarifications from procurement:

- CloudLeap's reseller expects an explicit 12% pass-through. They prefer this be a line item in the private-offer (marketplace rebate) rather than a separate manual rebate.
- We need the marketplace SKU anchors (exact SKU names/prices) so our finance team can map to their forecast models.
- DocuSign turnaround: if we can get a final PO + private-offer draft this week, procurement can sign within 3 business days.

We're comfortable with a conditional uplift in pass-through at $700k, but procurement wants the exact trigger definition (calendar vs trailing 12 months) and the verification method (HubSpot usage report vs marketplace billing).

If you can produce a draft private-offer PDF and marketplace SKU listing I can route to our legal.

Best,
Amy

(Procurement copied: procurement@cloudleap.com)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@cloudleap.com>, CloudLeap Procurement <procurement@cloudleap.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer structure and channel hurdle for CloudLeap – bundling options

Amy — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a concise private-offer terms PDF and the marketplace SKU anchor list for AWS and GCP. Highlights: 

- Year 1: 12% channel pass-through (marketplace rebate line item) applied to list price; applies from signature date.
- Uplift trigger: trailing 12-month ARR (HubSpot + marketplace billing reconciliation). If trailing ARR >= $700k at quarter boundary, pass-through increases to 14% starting next billing month. Verification: hubspot deal timeline + AWS/GCP usage export.
- SKU anchors: Hosted-API-US-1 (list $0.025/1k tokens), Reserved-Throughput-US-1 (list $9,500/month instance). Private-offer line items in attached PDF include the example private-offer discounts by tier.
- Turnaround: once DocuSign MPA + PO returned, private offer creation typically 3–7 business days for AWS, 5–10 for GCP.

Next steps (agreed):
1) CloudLeap countersign DocuSign PO (link below) with the $350k initial commit and indicated reseller pass-through line item.
2) Redwood will create AWS & GCP private offers and share marketplace offer IDs.
3) Quarterly reconciliation cadence; first reconciliation at 90 days to validate usage split.

Attachments: 20261005-cloudleap-private-offer-finalized-terms.pdf (PDF)
Related links: HubSpot deal https://app.hubspot.com/deals/987654/CL-4632, DocuSign sign link https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/a1b2c3-cloudleap-po

If procurement wants a short call to sign off on verification language, Ben and I are available tomorrow morning.

Best regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, GTM Partnerships
Redwood Inference
